parts.label: (b)
parts.stem:
The number of mitochondria differs from cell to cell. Cells also vary in size and volume.
Table 6.2 shows the mean number of mitochondria per cell, the mean cell volume and the mean number of mitochondria per $\mu\text{m}^3$ of three types of mammalian cells.
Table 6.2
| cell type | mean number of mitochondria per cell | mean cell volume /$\mu\text{m}^3$ | mean number of mitochondria per $\mu\text{m}^3$ |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| fat cell | 100 | 600000 | $0.17 \times 10^{-3}$ |
| heart cell | 2000 | 45000 | $44.44 \times 10^{-3}$ |
| liver cell | 2000 | 125000 | .................... |

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text:
Calculate the mean number of mitochondria per $\mu\text{m}^3$ for the liver cell.
Write your answer in Table 6.2.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Suggest reasons for the difference in mean number of mitochondria per $\mu\text{m}^3$ between the fat cell and the heart cell.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Suggest why it is difficult to compare the ability of the three types of cell to respire aerobically, based **only** on the mean number of mitochondria per cell.
